images.title: Nisha's five shapes in a line
images.purpose: Show the concept's puzzle solved: five boxes in a line holding a circle, a square, a triangle, a hexagon and a rectangle, with the four clues written above, so that each clue can be checked against the line.
images.composition: The four clues as text at the top, and below them a row of five numbered boxes, each holding one shape with its name under it.
images.exact_structure: Plain white frame, 1456 by 816. HEADING: the text Nisha's shapes in a line in bold dark #1F2937 sans-serif (48 px), left edge at x 198, about y 70. CLUES: four lines of dark text (34 px), left edge at x 198, at about y 150, 205, 260 and 315: (a) The circle is at the left end. / (b) The square is next to the circle. / (c) The triangle is between the square and the hexagon. / (d) The rectangle is to the right of the hexagon. FIVE BOXES in one row, each a white square 180 px by 180 px with a thin dark #2B2B2B outline (3 px) and slightly rounded corners, top edge at y 390 and bottom edge at y 570, left edges at x 198, 418, 638, 858 and 1078 (a gap of 40 px between boxes). Inside the boxes, left to right, one flat shape each, centred at y 480: box 1 a teal #0072B2 circle 120 px across, centre (288, 480); box 2 an amber #E69F00 square with side 110 px, corners (453, 425), (563, 425), (563, 535), (453, 535); box 3 a reddish purple #CC79A7 equilateral triangle with side 130 px, apex (728, 422), base corners (663, 535) and (793, 535); box 4 a green #009E73 regular hexagon with points at left and right, 130 px from point to point, centre (948, 480); box 5 a grey #6B7280 rectangle 140 px wide and 80 px high, corners (1098, 440), (1238, 440), (1238, 520), (1098, 520). All shapes have a thin dark outline (3 px). Under each box, centred on the box: its number 1, 2, 3, 4 and 5 in bold dark text (40 px) at y 610, and under the number its name in dark text (34 px) at y 660: circle, square, triangle, hexagon, rectangle. In all: 5 boxes, 5 shapes, 5 numbers, 5 names and 4 clue lines. Nothing else in the frame.
labels: (a) The circle is at the left end.
(b) The square is next to the circle.
(c) The triangle is between the square and the hexagon.
(d) The rectangle is to the right of the hexagon.
rejection: any count of objects, cells, ticks or rows that differs from the numbers stated in the spec
any text beyond the listed visible text, or any listed text misspelled or altered
any board name, publisher name, book title, page number or curriculum branding anywhere in the frame
a hyphen used in place of a minus sign on any labelled number
any count of boxes, shapes, numbers or clue lines that differs from the numbers stated in the spec
a shape in a box other than the one stated
a clue line that is missing or reworded
images.takeaway: Use the surest clue first and fill one place at a time: circle, square, triangle, hexagon, rectangle fits all four clues.
images.description: Five numbered boxes in a line holding a circle, a square, a triangle, a hexagon and a rectangle, with the four clues of the puzzle written above.
images.context: Concept image for Solving a Shape Puzzle with Clues. It shows the concept's own puzzle of five shapes and not a figure from your maths book.
images.teaching_notes: Cover the boxes and let the child place the shapes clue by clue, then lift the cover to check. The slip to watch is reading between as only somewhere between instead of directly between.

image_decisions.why: The five boxes with their shapes and the four clues are the mathematics: the child checks each clue against the line in the picture.
